content: 1. Bee LA, Dombrowski JC, Kerani R, and Golden MR conducted a study in 2014 to evaluate the impact of nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT) on the detection of extragenital gonorrhea and chlamydia infections among men who have sex with men (MSM) attending sexually transmitted disease (STD) clinics. Their findings were published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases. 2. Van Liere GA, Van Rooijen MS, Hoebe CJ, Heijman T, De Vries HJ, and Dukers-Muijrers NH investigated the prevalence and associated factors of rectal-only chlamydia and gonorrhea infections in women and MSM. Their 2015 study was published in PLOS One. 3. Gunn RA, O’Brien CJ, Lee MA, and Gilchick RA analyzed the value of testing multiple anatomic sites for gonorrhea screening among MSM in San Diego, California, between 1997 and 2003. Their findings were published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2008. 4. Wi TE, Ndowa FJ, Ferreyra C, Kelly-Cirino C, Taylor MM, Toskin I, and colleagues discussed the challenges and potential solutions for diagnosing sexually transmitted infections (STIs) in resource-limited settings. Their work was published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2019. 5. Aboud L, Xu Y, Chow EP, Wi T, Baggaley R, Mello MB, and colleagues conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis in 2021 to assess the diagnostic accuracy of pooling urine, anorectal, and oropharyngeal specimens for detecting Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae. Their findings were published in BMC Medicine. 6. Thammajaruk N, Promthong S, Posita P, Chumseng S, Nampaisan O, Srivachiraroj P, and colleagues evaluated the use of pooled oropharyngeal, rectal, and urine samples for point-of-care detection of Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae by lay providers in key population-led health services in Thailand. Their study was published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2020. 7. Sultan B, White JA, Fish R, Carrick G, Brima N, Copas A, and colleagues conducted the 3 in 1 study, which assessed the pooling of self-taken oropharyngeal, urethral, and rectal samples into a single specimen for detecting Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis in MSM. Their findings were published in the Journal of Clinical Microbiology in 2016. 8. Dean JA, Bell SFE, Coffey L, Debattista J, Badman S, Redmond AM, and colleagues demonstrated improved sensitivity when using pooled urine, oropharyngeal, and rectal specimens with a molecular assay for detecting chlamydia and gonorrhea near the point of care. Their study was published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2020. 9. Badman SG, Bell SFE, Dean JA, Lemoire J, Coffey L, Debattista J, and colleagues reported reduced sensitivity when using pooled urine, oropharyngeal, and rectal specimens with a molecular assay for detecting chlamydia and gonorrhea near the point of care. Their findings were published in Sexual Health in 2020. 10. Verougstraete N, Verbeke V, De Cannière AS, Simons C, Padalko E, and Coorevits L compared pooled versus single-site testing for Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae in female sex workers. Their study, published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2020, evaluated the effectiveness of these methods. 11. De Baetselier I, Vuylsteke B, Yaya I, Dagnra A, Diande S, Mensah E, and colleagues assessed a new pooling method using the GeneXpert instrument for STI detection in MSM in West Africa. Their findings were published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2020. 12. The World Health Organization (WHO) published consolidated guidelines in 2016 on the prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and care of HIV, viral hepatitis, and STIs for key populations. These guidelines emphasize principles such as human rights, gender equality, equity, inclusion, medical ethics, universal health coverage, and evidence-based public health. 13. Wilson JD, Wallace HE, Loftus-Keeling M, Ward H, Davies B, Vargas-Palacios A, and colleagues conducted the Swab-Yourself Trial with Economic Monitoring and Testing for Infections Collectively (SYSTEMATIC) study. This study compared the diagnostic accuracy and cost-effectiveness of analyzing rectal, oropharyngeal, and urogenital samples individually versus as pooled specimens for diagnosing gonorrhea and chlamydia. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2020. 14. Chernesky M, Jang D, Martin I, Arias M, Shah A, Smieja M, and colleagues evaluated the detection of Mycoplasma genitalium, Chlamydia trachomatis, and Neisseria gonorrhoeae using Aptima assays on self-obtained vaginal swabs and urine collected at home and in clinics. Their study was published in Sexually Transmitted Diseases in 2019. 15. Speers DJ, Chua IJ, Manuel J, and Marshall L investigated the detection of Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis from pooled rectal, oropharyngeal, and urine specimens in MSM. Their findings were published in Sexually Transmitted Infections in 2018. 16. Shaw J, Saunders JM, and Hughes G conducted a web-based survey of English sexual health services to explore attitudes toward and experiences with pooled sampling for STI testing. Their study was published in the International Journal of STD & AIDS in 2018. 17. De Baetselier I, Osbak KK, Smet H, Kenyon CR, and Crucitti T conducted a cross-sectional study in Belgium to evaluate the molecular detection of Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae in pooled oropharyngeal, anorectal, and urine samples versus single-site testing among MSM. Their findings were published in Acta Clinica Belgica in 2020. 18. The WHO released guidelines in 2016 for the treatment of Chlamydia trachomatis and Neisseria gonorrhoeae, providing evidence-based recommendations for managing these infections.
